managers.message_to_team: The memo says to put a mark on every cup during off-peak, so please do that and I’ll check once the rush is over. With eight or more people waiting, or if we’re short-staffed, you can skip it—keep the drive-thru moving and resume when the line clears.
managers.private_thought: The rush exception should protect our window time, but I’ll need to make sure we actually pick this up when business settles down.

managers.message_to_team: We’re eight to twelve deep at peak, so keep the line moving and skip notes while we’re slammed. Once it clears and we’re under six, add any quick mark to each cup; I’ll keep an eye on throughput first.
managers.private_thought: There’s no upside to slowing the rush for notes, and I’m not spending labor chasing them when the lobby empties out later.

managers.message_to_team: When it’s calm, let’s add a little note or doodle to cups if it feels natural—it can be a nice touch for folks settling in. During the class-change rush, focus on getting drinks out and taking care of each other; no one needs to scramble over a note.
managers.private_thought: I’d rather the team feel trusted than turn a warm gesture into one more thing to get judged on.

managers.message_to_team: Corporate wants a little mark on cups when things calm down; with that line, don't sweat it right now. Just do what you can once it eases up.
managers.private_thought: Nobody's checking this, and keeping the line moving matters more today.

managers.message_to_team: Once the line settles below six, please put any little mark or note on every cup—I’ll check during the quieter stretch. While we’re at eight or more, skip it and keep the line moving.
managers.private_thought: I want to show I’m following the memo, but I hope nobody thinks I’m making the rush harder over a smiley.

managers.message_to_team: When it eases up, throw a smiley or ‘enjoy’ on the cups if it’s not slowing you down. During this line, keep drinks moving—don’t hold up a traveler over a note.
managers.private_thought: Corporate can count marks on cups, but at this gate they’ll remember whether they made the flight, not whether we drew a heart.
